subject: SynapsePilot: defining acceptance signals & go/no-go ladder
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@synapsehealth.com>

Cc: tom.reed@synapsehealth.com, ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: SynapsePilot: defining acceptance signals & go/no-go ladder

Hi Priya / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo this week — the Synapse team is excited about the latency gains and the potential cost profile. Before we lock timelines with procurement, we need a compact MAP and a clear signal catalog we can share with our clinical QA and security reviewers.

High level asks from our side:
- A concise list of primary acceptance signals (what we measure) and hard exit gates (what fails the eval).
- A minimal set of acceptance tests we can run in our staging environment (sample prompts, pass/fail criteria).
- Clear owners and dates for each gate so we can schedule our internal risk review.

For scope: this pilot covers the Summarization and Triage flows only (no PHI ingestion for now). Key constraints from Synapse: 95th percentile inference latency <= 350ms for average prompt length, F1 >= 0.78 on our annotated triage set, and <2% hallucination rate on a curated hallucination suite.

I've attached an initial spreadsheet with our proposed scenarios (synapse-eval-scenarios.xlsx). Can your team propose a short runbook we can sign off on this week?

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
Director of Clinical Informatics
Synapse Health

Attachment: synapse-eval-scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12 rows)
From: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-10T13:45:00Z
Subject: Re: SynapsePilot: defining acceptance signals & go/no-go ladder

Maria — thanks for the clear asks and the spreadsheet, very helpful. I sketched a lean MAP + signal catalog you can distribute to QA and procurement; attaching a draft (MAP-draft-v1.docx). Key points in this draft (summary here so you don't have to open the doc):

1) Acceptance signal categories (what we'll measure):
   - Performance: 95th pct latency, avg tokens/sec, error rate (timeouts/failed inferences). Target: 95p <= 350ms, error rate <0.5%.
   - Quality: triage F1, summarization ROUGE-L (or human concordance sample). Target: F1 >= 0.78, avg human concordance >= 88%.
   - Safety/Hallucination: hallucination rate on curated suite; aim <2%. Any single catastrophic hallucination (PHI leakage or hallucination that could change clinical decision) is a hard fail.
   - Data handling: logs retention and KV cache policy; confirm no customer PHI persisted by default during pilot.

2) Exit gates (hard stop):
   - Any security audit failure (unresolved more-than-low severity finding).
   - Sustained 95p latency > 400ms across three consecutive runs.
   - Quality: F1 < 0.7 on triage benchmark after two remediation attempts.

3) Acceptance test suite (staged):
   - Smoke (2 days): basic throughput + sample prompts (10 prompts) — pass if no timeouts and basic labels match.
   - Functional (5 days): run curated triage set (n=500) and summarization concordance checks (n=200) — pass per thresholds above.
   - Adversarial (3 days): hallucination suite and boundary cases. Any catastrophic case triggers immediate pause.

4) Owners & timeline (proposed):
   - Redwood infra run: perf + latency (Priya) — 10/14 - 10/16
   - Redwood QA + Synapse clinical review: quality evals (Karthik + Maria) — 10/17 - 10/22
   - Consolidated sign-off: Synapse Risk & Redwood Sales — target 10/23

5) Artifacts to sign: MAP summary page, evidence catalog (spreadsheet), and a final runbook pdf.

Next steps: if this aligns with Synapse's internal calendar I can lock a final MAP and schedule the test windows. I've also added a short procurement checklist in the draft to make budget sign-off smoother.

Best,
Priya Natarajan

1) For the hallucination hard-fail definition, can you add an explicit example in the runbook (e.g., hallucinated medication names or fabricated clinical findings)?
2) We need one shared artifact: a short evidence catalog with exact input IDs we ran and an exportable CSV of model outputs for audit.
